simple.meaning: זוּד (zûwd) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be proud.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 5:20. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זוּד (H2103) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: זוּד (zûwd) / H2103 is traced through Daniel 5:20 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2103. zud [ זוּד ] verb be presumptuous ( ᵑ7 J ; see Biblical Hebrew [ זוּד זִיד, ]); — Haph`el Infinitive לַהֲוָדָה Dan 5:20 act presumptuously.

occurrences.englishText: But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him.
